safety_lead_time.comparison_action: REDUCE — SAP safety lead time of 3.0 days is excessive given a mean lead time of 0.98 days; recommend reducing to 1.32 days

narrative: Material PL1__M84A42A1 exhibits moderate daily demand averaging 1,894 units with a CV of 0.45, punctuated by intermittent zero-demand days (approx. 9% of working days) and occasional demand spikes. Lead times are highly variable (CV = 0.935, range 0.11–4.94 days), making lead-time variability the dominant uncertainty driver at 81% of total sigma_LTD. The current SAP policy holds zero safety stock and orders at the bare MOQ (2,174 units), generating ~218 orders per year with significant stockout risk. The optimized (r,Q) policy increases the batch to the EOQ of 11,713 units, establishes a 3,171-unit safety buffer at 95% service level, reduces annual ordering events by 82%, and cuts total cost by 54% — all within the 24,563-unit storage capacity.
warnings: Lead time CV = 0.935 indicates highly unstable supplier delivery; monitor supplier KPIs
12 demand outliers detected and winsorized at 99th percentile
SAP safety lead time of 3.0 days is significantly higher than recommended 1.32 days — review with procurement

research_insights.selection_rationale: With near-continuous, moderately variable demand (CV=0.45) and short but highly variable lead times (mean=0.98 days, CV=0.935), a continuous-review (r,Q) policy is optimal. It responds immediately to inventory drawdowns without periodic review lag, and the fixed order quantity at EOQ minimises total ordering-plus-holding cost. The MOQ of 2,174 units is non-binding as EOQ (11,713) substantially exceeds it.
research_insights.boundary_risk: Storage capacity is non-binding: safety_stock (3,171) + order_quantity (11,713) = 14,884 units vs. limit of 24,563 units, leaving 9,679 units of spare capacity. No capacity-driven service degradation expected.
